gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to the conclusion that the project was not viable.
gaps.explanation: come to the conclusion that ... is the fixed phrase; 'reach' and 'arrive' do not take 'to'.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to prison for ___ the law.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'the law' (opposite of obeying it)
gaps.explanation: break the law means to commit a crime; after the preposition 'for' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ sure that all the windows are locked.
gaps.explanation: make sure means to check that something is true or has been done.

gaps.sentence: Grandad's best man ___ a joke that made everyone laugh.
gaps.explanation: tell a joke is the fixed collocation; 'say a joke' is not used.

gaps.sentence: Her talk really ___ home the urgency of the situation.
gaps.explanation: 'Drive something home' = make it fully understood.
